Lessons.Title: Attributes that Define Shapes
ExplanationParagraphs: 2021 Grade3 Unit7 Lesson3 public teacher lesson.html SHA256 20aba2c371feac123b29df724edb270a0a33e242df0478cd9f567acc66a18d75 and preparation.html SHA256 7ae37382d333500f19850c2d46d349ac863ea09a36c085150bb0ebf72fbfa7c9 were read from the local source archive. Three pupil sections were reviewed. Publisher original source Quadrilateral Cards blackline/master pixels, standalone Student Task PDF, first-party live browser and gated Cool-down Mystery Shape were not inspected. This is documented source-semantic teaching content with teacher-visual gates rather than source-art parity.

Original warm-up Number Talk Multiply Multiples of Ten (10 min) has four exact computations:4×40=160,8×40=320,7×40=280,9×40=360. Use known four-times multiplication facts and grouping by tens, noting 8×40 doubles4×40 and7×40 is one group40 below8×40. Teacher may accept varied reasoning even though four numeric results are fixed.

Activity1 Learn How to Play Mystery Quadrilateral (10 min) is a TEACHER MODEL of a complete original rule cycle. Teacher secretly places ONE QUADRILATERAL card from preceding U07:L02 inside a folder. Class plays Partner B and may ask UP TO FIVE questions each answered YES or NO about geometric attributes. Class then guesses, teacher reveals the actual card, and class discusses which questions usefully eliminated possibilities. Source student instructions additionally say switch roles and play again; classroom demonstration can model this.

Activity2 Play Mystery Quadrilateral (25 min) is a DISTINCT second activity using PAIRS. Each pair receives the same set of quadrilateral shape cards carried from the previous lesson, a folder to hide the selected card, and access to printed cards/workbook figures to mark or COVER eliminated shapes with counters. Partner A chooses and hides a shape unseen; Partner B asks NO MORE THAN FIVE YES/NO attribute questions, then guesses; A reveals; partners SWITCH ROLES and play again. The hidden selection is intentionally variable, so no one predetermined correct card is legitimate.

Good source questions focus on geometric ATTRIBUTES, such as 'Are all four sides the same length?', 'Does the shape have a right angle?', 'Are exactly two sides equal?' rather than naming a shape immediately ('Is it a square?'). Both yes and no eliminate plausible cards; make strategic questions narrowing remaining possibilities. Grade3 teacher encourages using side/angle/right-angle/equal/slanted/tall/skinny vocabulary without falsely asserting angle degrees not supplied by source.

The original pupil textbook carries a display of quadrilaterals for elimination, but independent source blackline card geometry was not inspected: teacher must verify card identities and yes/no responses against actual source illustrations. No fabricated fixed guessed quadrilateral or card-specific answer key is added. Original source synthesis displays S, U and X cards and asks how shared quadrilateral features can be distinguished by number of equal-length sides and right angles; geometry of letters S/U/X not certified without the source figures.

Teacher supports MLR8 discussion, counters to cover eliminated candidates and peer role collaboration. Two mathematically correct players may pursue different five-question sequences; evaluate truthfulness, informative property questions, sensible elimination and explanation. Restricted publisher Cool-down Mystery Shape not retrieved. Source PDF/pixel parity, new tests, CI, academic Stage D and production release unverified.

KeyConcepts.Title: Quadrilateral properties
KeyConcepts.Definition: A quadrilateral has four sides and can be distinguished by side lengths and types of corners.
KeyConcepts.Example: Does the shape have right angles?

KeyConcepts.Title: Five YES/NO-question limit
KeyConcepts.Definition: Only up to five yes/no questions may be asked before final guess.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Ask<=5, then guess, show and switch roles.
KeyConcepts.Example: Questions about matching side lengths eliminate candidate cards.

KeyConcepts.Title: Secret shape choice
KeyConcepts.Definition: Partner A privately chooses card, so the correct letter varies from round to round.
KeyConcepts.Rule: A truthful answer depends on actual chosen quadrilateral.
KeyConcepts.Example: One student can choose a four-right-angle shape and another a slanted parallelogram.

KeyConcepts.Title: Evidence-based elimination
KeyConcepts.Definition: Each verified answer can rule out shapes whose properties conflict.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Eliminate only cards inconsistent with yes/no evidence.
KeyConcepts.Example: If selected shape has no right angles, remove right-angled candidates.

WorkedExamples.Title: Teacher example of useful questions
WorkedExamples.Question: Why ask about an attribute before naming the shape?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use one answer to remove many cards.
Steps: Ask whether all sides have same length.
Compare yes/no result to visible source cards.
Continue up to five then guess.
WorkedExamples.Check: Original outcome depends on actual source-selected card.

WorkedExamples.Title: Original pair turn-taking
WorkedExamples.Question: When is a round finished?
Steps: B asks up to five yes/no questions.
WorkedExamples.Answer: After guess, reveal and swap roles
WorkedExamples.Check: Original teacher demonstration and peer game are separate activities.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Ask unlimited yes/no questions until all but one candidate remains.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Original student text limits each round to up to FIVE.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Count questions and make final guess after maximum five.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treat the answer as a predetermined card letter.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Partner A chooses any permitted shape secretly.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Teacher checks actual hidden card and the evidence.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Run only teacher demonstration and omit peer rounds.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Original source has two separate activities, peer play is second.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Preserve pair round, guessing/reveal and role switch.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Ask for formal shape names rather than properties.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Teacher emphasizes attribute language over immediate name guesses.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Ask about equal sides or right angles.

SummaryPoints: Activity1 teacher demo, Activity2 partner game; original Quadrilateral Cards reused from U07:L02, hidden in folders, counters help eliminate.
Partner B may ask UP TO FIVE yes/no QUESTIONS, then GUESS; partner A reveals, partners SWITCH roles and repeat.
Teacher checks actual variable card attributes and strategy; no fixed card answer or false blackline-art parity.
Original source PDF and publisher Cool-down not inspected; tests and Stage D not executed.
